cues.zh: 我思考这个问题有一段时间了，我得出的结论是，我们在计算机科学和计算领域对工程概念有着这种情感上的依恋。这很大程度上源于软件工程运动之类的事物。我们有点宣称自己不再属于那个领域了，但其实我们依然属于。我们的经验深受其影响。事实上，我们拥有的是一种最佳实践的迷信。事实上，现在几乎每个人都在崇拜……

Well, through the ages of developing and working with our software, problems have shown up, driven by the machine. And we've invented our own spaces, our worlds, our programming languages that allow us to live in these worlds. But the ideas that are driving these programming languages are driven by the machine. We're living in a world designed by the machine.

cues.en: talked about in his Turing Award lecture. He framed them all in terms of these two quotes. He set the stage with these two quotes. cues.zh: 在他的图灵奖演讲中谈到的设计原则。他用这两段引文来框定它们全部。他用这两段引文做铺垫。这些引文讲的是记法的力量：它能影响人的能力，尤其是心智能力，去应对问题和复杂性。为了把这一点具体化、落到实处，他提出了一套他认为好的记法应当具备的原则。APL 是一种记法。注意，我这里真正关注的是人。

cues.en: Keep that in mind. So with APL, what we're aiming for is ease of solution expression. That means the degree to which problems find a suitable and easy expression in our language natively. Suggestivity is really one of my favorites. It's the degree to which, when you write some piece of code, that code inspires you, suggests alternatives, patterns, ways of looking at things. It's not just about seeing what's there, but seeing how that
cues.zh: 记住这一点。所以在 APL 中，我们追求的是解决方案表达的容易度。也就是说，问题能在我们的语言中原生地找到合适而简单表达的程度。暗示性是我最喜欢的原则之一。它指的是：当你写某段代码时，这段代码能启发你，提示替代方案、模式、看待事物的方式的程度。这不只是看到那里有什么，而是看到那个

cues.en: Thing that you're looking at that piece of code could apply elsewhere. Maybe it in Suggests that you look at a different type of code or a different approach or you see connections and patterns. It's about recognizing the bigger picture and to do that we need to Subordinate detail, but not abstraction abstraction is hiding away detail and pretending it doesn't exist. This is letting ourselves
cues.zh: 你正在看的那个东西——那段代码——还能应用到哪里。也许它暗示你去看另一种代码、另一种方法，或者让你看到联系和模式。这关乎识别更大的图景，而要做到这一点，我们需要让细节从属，但不是抽象——抽象是把细节藏起来，假装它不存在。这是让我们自己

cues.en: know the detail exists, but subordinating it so it does not introduce an increased mental cognitive load. And economy is an important element because economy is how much it takes to actually get to the solution. So it's not how neat does your little solution look once you've built up all of your frameworks and your libraries and everything else. It's how much, how big is your vocabulary to solve so many problems.
cues.zh: 知道细节存在，但把它置于次要位置，这样它就不会增加心智认知负担。而经济性是一个重要因素，因为经济性是你实际得到解决方案需要付出多少代价。所以，它不是在你搭好所有框架、库和其他东西之后，你那小解决方案看起来多整洁。它是你的词汇量有多大、多丰富，能解决这么多问题。

cues.en: As the more problems you solve, does your library get bigger? Or can you solve a whole lot of problems with a very small vocabulary and a very small set of tools without needing to build up a lot of libraries and frameworks and other things? An economical language will get you further with less than a language that requires you to build a lot of extra abstractions. And then finally, we saw the amenability to formal proofs. I don't think there's any necessary need to belabor that point because Roger demonstrated that fairly convincingly. You...
cues.zh: 随着你解决的问题越来越多，你的库会变得越来越大吗？还是说，你可以用非常小的词汇量和非常少的一组工具解决大量问题，而不必构建大量库、框架和其他东西？一种经济的语言，比一种要求你构建大量额外抽象的语言，更能让你事半功倍。最后，我们还看到了它对形式化证明的适用性。我觉得没必要在这一点上过多展开，因为 Roger 已经相当有说服力地证明了这一点。你……

cues.en: APL is great for pushing symbols around, for thinking algebraically about your code as a whiteboard language, right? You want that kind of thing. So, how do we get from there to how do I actually program with this? Well, basically, you're doing it wrong, and what I've developed is a set of patterns and anti-patterns. The problem is, as computer scientists, we...
cues.zh: APL 非常适合推演符号，也适合用代数方式思考代码，把它当作一种白板语言，对吧？你需要的就是这种感觉。那么，我们该如何从这里走到“我到底该怎么用它编程”呢？基本上，你现在的做法是错的，而我总结出了一套模式和反模式。问题在于，作为计算机科学家，我们……

cues.en: I've embedded these ideas, these best practices in our heads and how we need to approach problems. And those are now anti-patterns in APL. Good APL tends to exhibit design principles that are diametrically opposed to the way you've been told how to write good code. And this is a problem. Because every time you go to write good code, you're making decisions implicitly that you might not even realize based on those patterns. And so to write good APL code, I suggest...
cues.zh: 我已经把这些理念和最佳实践内化到我们的思维中，也内化成了我们处理问题的方式。而在 APL 里，它们如今反而成了反模式。优秀的 APL 往往体现出一些设计原则，而这些原则与你一直被告知的优秀代码写法截然相反。这就是问题所在。因为每当你准备写出“优秀代码”时，你都会下意识地根据那些模式做出决定，甚至可能根本没有意识到这一点。所以，要写出优秀的 APL 代码，我建议……

cues.en: sticking with a new set of patterns, and I've got eight of them here. Now, these aren't rules. These are principles that are going to drive your thought process, and they'll each be manifested for a given type of problem in a different way. So these aren't rules. These are spectrums of possibility that open up because of the notation we have. And in addition to this, it's interesting to wonder, well, is this intuitive? Is this natural?
cues.zh: 继续采用一套新的模式，这里我有八个。这些不是规则，而是驱动你思考过程的原则，每种原则会在不同类型的问题中以不同方式体现。所以它们不是规则，而是因为我们的表示法而开启的可能性光谱。除此之外，有趣的是想一想，这直观吗？自然吗？

cues.en: So I'm going to be referencing Miller 1981 and Payne 2001, which are two studies that were conducted with non-programmers in an attempt to see when given a programming task, natural language like English, and no programming background, how did they describe the process of programming to other people? What is the normal human way, the natural programming model that humans work with before they've been trained in computer science?
cues.zh: 我将引用Miller 1981和Payne 2001，这两项研究是针对非程序员进行的，试图了解当给定一个编程任务、使用像英语这样的自然语言、且没有编程背景时，他们如何向他人描述编程过程？在受过计算机科学训练之前，人类正常的做事方式、自然的编程模型是什么？

cues.en: I suppose brevity over verbosity. And I think most people think that short code is good, but they don't really actually like short code. They tend to associate short code with cleverness, and that is a bad thing. You want your code to be stupid. But brevity is really about finding simple, natural, easy, short expressions that we can work with. So let's consider a nice, simple, basic example, your average function.
cues.zh: 我想是简洁胜于冗长。我认为大多数人觉得短代码好，但他们其实并不真正喜欢短代码。他们往往把短代码与聪明联系起来，而那是坏事。你希望你的代码是愚蠢的。但简洁真正关乎找到简单、自然、易于使用的短表达式。所以让我们考虑一个简单的基本例子，普通函数。

cues.en: So this is an expression in APL. It's a definition for a function that computes the average of a vector, say. So now, if you're in a functional programming language, you probably do something similar to this. Maybe a fold reduction with plus over the list divided by the count. That's basically what this is doing. All right, seems pretty good. But now, I want to do this with an arbitrary number of samples that I've taken. So I've done sampling multiple times.
cues.zh: 这是APL中的一个表达式。它是一个函数的定义，用来计算一个向量的平均值。所以如果你在函数式编程语言中，你可能会做类似的事情。也许是列表上的加法折叠归约除以计数。这基本上就是它所做的。好，看起来不错。但现在，我想用任意数量的样本来做这个。所以我已经多次采样了。

cues.en: And I want to get the average of each of that group of samples. Now, how do you have to adapt your program? What do you have to do? Well, you probably need to figure out whether you're going to do a zip or a map, another map or another thing. In APL, well, no, we don't do that. We just leave it as is, because it already works for that as well. And so we've kept things short. And the reason we keep things short, the method behind the madness, is our code is bigger on the inside than on the outside. And this allows us to do a lot of interesting things.
cues.zh: 我想求这组样本中每个样本的平均值。现在，你该如何修改你的程序？你需要做什么？嗯，你可能得琢磨着用 zip 还是 map，再加一个 map 或是别的什么。但在 APL 里，不用，我们不需要那样做。我们直接保持原样就行，因为它本来就支持这种操作。所以我们保持了代码的简短。我们保持代码简短的原因——这种疯狂背后的逻辑——是我们的代码“外表小巧，内涵乾坤”。这让我们能够做很多有趣的事情。

cues.en: One of the biggest things is that it keeps our code malleable. It's easier to work with. It's easier to tweak and play with. We can really move it around like clay. And one of the reasons we can do this is because we have more confidence in our code, because the code can fit in our heads. And this is something that's important. You want your code to fit in your brain. And APL is one of the few languages where your average APL, or you go to him and ask, what's your favorite program? He'll write his favorite program down from memory. He's got...
cues.zh: 其中最重要的一点是，它让我们的代码具有极佳的可塑性。用起来更轻松。调整和把玩也更容易。我们真的可以像玩泥巴一样随意揉捏它。之所以能做到这一点，原因之一是我们对代码更有信心，因为代码能够装进我们的大脑。这一点非常重要。你希望你的代码能装进你的脑子里。APL 是极少数能让你随性而为的语言之一，如果你去找一个 APL 程序员，问他最喜欢的程序是什么？他能凭记忆把程序写下来。他的脑子里装着……

cues.en: programs in his memory. How many of you could, without looking at your computer, sit down and write without bugs in it, your program, favorite program, an actual program, a real whole thing that does a real useful piece of work? You just don't do that in other programming languages. It's an advantage of brevity that people overlook. So what do the studies say? Well, the studies have found that universally, people were annoyed if they felt like they had to be too verbose.
cues.zh: 各种程序。你们当中有谁能不看电脑，坐下来就能毫无 bug 地写出你的程序、你最喜欢的程序——一个真正的、完整的、能完成一个真正有用任务的程序？在其他编程语言里你根本做不到这一点。这是人们往往忽视的简洁带来的优势。那么研究是怎么说的呢？嗯，研究发现，普遍而言，如果人们觉得代码必须写得太啰嗦，都会感到烦恼。

cues.en: They always wanted to try to create shortcuts and create shorter and shorter descriptions. And it's just a natural human tendency because it's a type of optimization that we want to do when we're engaging with process. So let's look at the next pattern, macro over micro. I think we can clearly think about this by looking at some pictures. So here's some beautiful bark, excellent picture, wonderful design, micro view, right? We can really see what's going on in this picture.
cues.zh:
他们总是想方设法走捷径，创造越来越简短的描述。
@@
这只是一种人类的自然倾向，因为这是我们在参与某个流程时想要进行的一种优化。
@@

我们真的能看清这张图里发生了什么。

cues.en: We've got control, right? I mean, if I need to deal with these pieces of bark, I've got it. The problem is we've missed the frickin' mountain that's about to come crashing down on us or that we have to deal with. And so the APL are, yeah, maybe we don't see the bark, but we get to see that mountain. We can plan for it. We can deal with it. We can make decisions at a macro level. And that's what you need to try to do when you're code, when you're working with APL. You want to try to look at that global view, that whole thing.
cues.zh: 我们能掌控局面，对吧？我是说，如果我要处理这些树皮，我没问题。问题在于，我们漏掉了那座该死的、快要砸到我们头上、或者我们必须应对的大山。所以，APL 嘛——是啊，也许我们看不到树皮，但我们能看到那座山。我们可以为它做计划。我们可以应对它。我们可以在宏观层面做决策。这就是你在写代码、使用 APL 时要努力做到的事。你要试着看全局，看整体。

cues.en: I want to think of everything and encompass everything rather than going element by element or item or item. Look at your problem and your architecture and the way the big picture fits together and make optimizations there so that you don't need to make premature optimizations inside the micro level of your code. So as an example of this, we have this partitioning function or using a hash function to do a partition and compute over the elements partitioned by some categorizer. So we've got alpha here.
cues.zh: 我想从整体思考、涵盖所有内容，而不是逐元素、逐项处理。审视你的问题和架构，看大局如何契合，在那里做优化，这样就不必在代码微观层面做过早优化。举个例子，我们有个分区函数，或者用哈希函数来做分区，并按某种分类器对分区后的元素进行计算。这里我们有 alpha。

cues.en: That's our hash function or our hashing function. It'll partition everything that we want to work with. And to an APLer, it's immediately obvious what the big picture is here. It's that giant square. And it informs everything that we're doing. We can see that big picture. Notice that we haven't cluttered this up with micro-questions about iterations, loops, anything like that. We've used a nice, easy-to-identify symbol that clearly defines our access patterns and gives us the big picture. And then we've sort of, we let the rest of it happen.
cues.zh: 这就是我们的哈希函数，或者说散列函数。它会把我们要处理的一切都划分开。而对 APL 程序员来说，这里的大局一眼就清楚。就是那个巨大的方块。它为我们所做的一切提供依据。我们能看到这个大局。注意，我们没有用关于迭代、循环之类的微观问题把它搞乱。我们用一个漂亮、易于识别的符号，清楚地定义访问模式，并给出大局。然后我们就，某种程度上，让剩下的部分自然发生。

cues.en: And we don't worry about some of these microview questions. So, what do the studies say? Well, I think it's pretty self-explanatory. When people program and they don't know how to program, they tend to vastly prefer to talk about big picture things using giant sets of things. They almost never use the singular. They always talk about the plural, about groups of things, sets of things, and they use aggregate operations. Sound like the language we're talking about?
cues.zh: 我们不必担心其中一些微观视角的问题。那么研究怎么说？嗯，我觉得这相当不言自明。当人们编程、而他们并不会编程时，他们往往非常喜欢用巨大的集合来谈论大局问题。他们几乎从不使用单数。他们总是谈复数、谈一组组东西、一堆堆东西，并且使用聚合操作。听起来像我们正在谈论的语言吗？
